bug_semantics: Genkit's unauthenticated developer servers listened beyond a loopback-only trust boundary and did not validate the HTTP Host header. A LAN peer, or a website using DNS rebinding, could reach the Tools/Dev UI or reflection runAction handler, execute registered actions with attacker-controlled input and context, and read results. The telemetry trace SSE handler also set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, exposing trace data. CORS was not an authorization gate because it did not prevent handler execution and DNS rebinding made the request same-origin to the attacker's page.
flaw_origin: The earliest public carrier is squash aggregate 91ed3de52e7db92943886526395ad8eac6faa77f. Its parent 805600159f34ca96d95c26c10c7b2799cb5951ce had only the stub Runner server and no runAction or reflection execution path; the aggregate adds an unauthenticated Runner runAction proxy, a reflection /api/runAction executor, and listeners without host arguments or Host validation. The aggregate message enumerates 27 squashed member changes, including 'Added basic Reflection API', 'Added starting of app code when starting Runner API', and 'Implemented passthrough endpoints in Runner API'. Those unavailable member objects must be distinguished to identify the smallest commit that first completed the exploitable path, so the aggregate itself is not accepted as the BIC.
ai_marker: unavailable: git cat-file -p 91ed3de52e7db92943886526395ad8eac6faa77f shows human author Alex Pascal, GitHub committer, one parent, and no AI/bot/co-author/generated trailer, but 91ed3de52e7db92943886526395ad8eac6faa77f is only the squash aggregate. The true introducing member commit object is absent, so BIC-only author, committer, trailers, and bot identity cannot be inspected and the aggregate's metadata is not substituted.
evidence: Origin and parent were rechecked in the validated clone. git cat-file -p 91ed3de52e7db92943886526395ad8eac6faa77f reports parent 805600159f34ca96d95c26c10c7b2799cb5951ce and the 27-item squash message. git grep -n -E 'runAction|startReflectionApi' 805600159f34ca96d95c26c10c7b2799cb5951ce -- genkit-tools genkit/common returns no match, while the same tree query on 91ed3de52e7db92943886526395ad8eac6faa77f finds genkit-tools/src/runner/router.ts runAction, api.listen(port), genkit/common/src/reflectionApi.ts /api/runAction, and api.listen(numericPort). For the assigned fix_sha disagreement, the primary recorded fix_sha null but direct_fix_sha fb00011b5aade16638c9f6b72502e2085d94ca51; the reviewer recorded both null. The reviewer wins. Git show proves landed commit 66bfbbc5198db40e236d61760ea5ab2b34aac75c only changes the Tools, telemetry, and reflection listeners to bind 127.0.0.1. git grep finds no rejectNonLoopbackHost at that commit, while it still finds telemetry-server/src/index.ts setting Access-Control-Allow-Origin to '*'. git tag --contains 66bfbbc5198db40e236d61760ea5ab2b34aac75c --list 'genkit-cli@*' starts at genkit-cli@1.40.0; genkit-cli@1.39.0 resolves to 54c60aab1c89844e0ba6231f46f9a13241e6368c and 1.40.0 to c85153e04c766300fa2fdd755393076657f2a216. The latest checked release genkit-cli@1.42.0, 47a301141d8f3ca04e870e8d21bcaab293927e15, and main still have no rejectNonLoopbackHost and still set wildcard trace SSE CORS, so the released change blocks direct LAN access but not the advisory's DNS-rebinding/Host-header mechanism. The current GitHub advisory still says 'Fixed on 2026-06-18' but lists no vulnerable package/version ranges. GitHub's PR API reports advisory-linked #5587 open, merged_at null, merge_commit_sha null. Its commit API shows fb00011b5aade16638c9f6b72502e2085d94ca51 fixes only Tools/telemetry; its child 34ec0a6ca0bfc7b2caedd7524939779556317da0 adds reflection Host validation. git for-each-ref --contains for both commits returns no local, remote, or tag ref. Thus fb00011b5aade16638c9f6b72502e2085d94ca51 is neither landed nor a complete fix for all affected execution surfaces, and 34ec0a6ca0bfc7b2caedd7524939779556317da0 is only the unmerged second source patch, not an upstream fix or direct commit underlying a landed fix.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first tracing places the exploitable capability between the public trees at 805600159f34ca96d95c26c10c7b2799cb5951ce and 91ed3de52e7db92943886526395ad8eac6faa77f, but protocol rejects the latter because it is a squash aggregate. The unavailable member history prevents the smallest-BIC parent test and BIC-object AI attribution, so BLOCKED remains gate-complete. On the fix dispute, loopback binding is only partial mitigation: a DNS-rebinding hostname can resolve to loopback while preserving a non-loopback Host value, and without Host validation the action handler remains reachable; wildcard telemetry CORS also remains. The advisory's date-only assertion is contradicted by repository state and the still-open remediation PR. The primary's fb00011b5aade16638c9f6b72502e2085d94ca51 direct-fix claim is rejected because that unmerged first PR commit omits the reflection server fixed by its child 34ec0a6ca0bfc7b2caedd7524939779556317da0. The reviewer correctly leaves both fix fields null because no complete remediation has landed or shipped.
remaining_gap: Recover the original squashed PR #3 member commit that first completed the runnable unauthenticated action path, its immediate parent, and that BIC commit object's author/committer/trailers. The full vulnerability is also still unpatched upstream as of 2026-08-28: released 66bfbbc5198db40e236d61760ea5ab2b34aac75c is only loopback-binding hardening, and the complete Host-validation/CORS source series through 34ec0a6ca0bfc7b2caedd7524939779556317da0 remains in open PR #5587 rather than a landed commit or release.
